SYSTEM_FALSE_NEGATIVE_LLM_NONE.prompt_deficiency_found: The model was given only each Alpha's one-sentence abstract core_thesis, never its trigger_signals/confirmation_signals -- concrete, already-authored example manifestations. With only an abstract sentence to match against, paraphrased, indirect, or company-specific phrasing (never restating the thesis in the Alpha's own words) plausibly reads as not 'directly and substantively' engaging any Alpha, biasing the model toward decision=none.

SYSTEM_FALSE_POSITIVE_OVERMATCH.prompt_deficiency_found: The existing v3 prompt already told the model to use none for 'generic or background market commentary,' but gave no explicit guidance on the specific recurring failure pattern observed: a bare, standalone financial figure or ratio (an EPS number, a valuation multiple, an asset-value estimate) with no stated causal mechanism, which the model was nonetheless attributing to a loosely valuation- or growth-adjacent Alpha.

OTHER_WRONG_ALPHA_SUBSTITUTION.prompt_deficiency_found: Same root deficiency as the false-negative category (abstract-thesis-only comparison starves the model's own existing 'compare mechanisms directly' instruction of the concrete signal it needs to discriminate well between two plausible Alphas).

CROSS_FAMILY_GROWTH_VS_RISK_CONFUSION.prompt_deficiency_found: Same root deficiency as above, applied to growth-vs-risk-family neighbor pairs specifically.

A101_A102_A103_BOUNDARY_CONFUSION.prompt_deficiency_found: Same root deficiency as above. Also noted: these 2 samples predate commit c454245's v3 A101/A103 worked example, so part of this specific pair's confusion is independently explained by prompt age (see v0_2_semantic_reproducibility_audit.json), not solely by the missing trigger/confirmation signal data addressed here.

changes_applied.change: Added trigger_signals and confirmation_signals (already-existing AlphaDefinition fields, sourced from alpha_taxonomy_v1.yaml, never fabricated) to each taxonomy entry in the request payload, alongside the existing alpha_id/alpha_name/definition.
changes_applied.generalization: Applies automatically to the full taxonomy and to both the single-claim and batched classifier call sites (both consume this same function) -- not ticker-specific, not sample-specific, adds zero new Alpha IDs.

changes_applied.change: Added two symmetric, general instruction sentences (identical in both, preserving the existing 'copied verbatim' invariant between the single and batched variants): (1) treat trigger_signals/confirmation_signals as positive evidence even under paraphrase, without requiring literal keyword overlap with the abstract definition; (2) a bare standalone financial figure/ratio is never sufficient alone -- only select when the evidence connects it to a specific Alpha's own mechanism/trigger/confirmation signal.
changes_applied.generalization: Both sentences are taxonomy-wide rules referencing Alpha-structural concepts (trigger_signals, confirmation_signals, 'a specific Alpha's own mechanism'), never a sample ID, holdout-specific phrase, or ticker name.

changes_applied.change: Bumped prompt_version (v3->v4, batch v1->v2) and input_schema_version (v2->v3, batch v1->v2) per this codebase's own ADR-005 convention: a versioned identifier must change with the instructions/contract it identifies, so no old cached pre-remediation result is ever silently reused as if it reflected the new prompt. output_schema_version unchanged (response contract itself did not change).

Both tests hardcoded the pre-remediation literal prompt text / version-identifier strings as fixtures. Updated both to reference the live _TASK_INSTRUCTIONS / _TASK_RUNTIME_METADATA source constants instead of a duplicated, now-stale copy -- preserves each test's full original assertion strength (still checks byte-exact prompt assembly / exact cache-key revalidation behavior) while tracking future deliberate, versioned prompt revisions instead of going stale against them. No assertion was weakened or removed.
